facts.statement: The genus Maroccosuchus was described by Jonet and Wouters in 1977.
Maroccosuchus zennaroi is an extinct gavialoid crocodylian found in Morocco.
facts.quote: Maroccosuchus zennaroi is an extinct gavialoid crocodylian from the Early Eocene of Morocco

facts.statement: Maroccosuchus is traditionally classified as a member of the subfamily Tomistominae.
facts.quote: traditionally regarded as a member of the subfamily Tomistominae

facts.statement: Recent molecular studies suggest that Tomistominae, including Maroccosuchus, actually belong to Gavialoidea and Gavialidae rather than being crocodiles.
facts.quote: recent molecular studies using DNA sequencing have consistently indicated that the false gharial (Tomistoma) (and by inference other related extinct forms in Tomistominae) actually belong to Gavialoidea (and Gavialidae)

facts.statement: Cladograms indicate Maroccosuchus is an early-diverging gavialoid, more basal than the common ancestor of gharials and false gharials.
facts.quote: shows Maroccosuchus as an early-diverging gavialoid, more basal than the last common ancestor to both the gharial and the false gharial

facts.statement: Maroccosuchus lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are currently three recorded fossil occurrences of Maroccosuchus.
